articles.title: Oversized Fashion Items Take Center Stage at Latest Collections
articles.summary: Designers such as Chanel and Acne Studios are showcasing oversized bags, jewelry, and accessories for fall/winter 2026.
articles.content: The world of fashion has seen a dramatic shift towards supersized bags, jewelry, and accessories. Recently, Rosalía was spotted walking through New York City streets with a bag from Dana Toder that measured over three feet long. The focus on these oversized items is evident in the latest collections from top designers such as Chanel, Acne Studios, and Bottega Veneta, who showcased their own versions for fall/winter 2026. However, it's Toder's extreme size and concept that take this trend to a new level. Designers are not only pushing the boundaries with oversized bags but also with jewelry and accessories. Chandelier earrings and necklaces have never been bigger, with Saint Laurent and Valentino leading the way. This emphasis on grandeur is taking everyday objects and turning them into statements of style. The creative process behind this trend can be seen in the work of Dana Toder, who originally designed her "Baggage Bag" for a fashion film called Krähe, directed by Lili Conzen and set to be released in spring 2027. The film's concept resonated deeply with Dana Toder, whose perspective on clothes and accessories is shaped by their emotional significance in a person's life. This connection was sparked when Lili Conzen shared her vision for the film, which explores who gets to be seen in fashion. The project's focus on giving older women leading roles highlights its aim to redefine traditional beauty standards. Toder sees a woman's relationship with her bag or garments as complex and emotionally charged. For her, this bond is not just about physical attachment but also metaphorical weight. This dual interpretation of baggage reflects the idea that our possessions carry more than just material value, they hold memories and emotions. The big bag featured in the film showcases the shared experience across different women, ages, and times through its unique print design. Combining analog photographs taken by the designer, director, and actresses in the film, it represents a visual representation of their collective stories. These images span decades from the 80s to the present day. The big bag's design plays a significant role in highlighting the emotional connection people have with their belongings. Toder notes that everything attached to a bag, what it holds, where it's been, and how its material changes over time, becomes emotionally significant. This perspective is reflected not just in the bag itself but also in the women who carry it. The sight of a woman rummaging through her oversized bag is a familiar one, with items spilling out in all directions as she searches for something specific. It's almost as if the act of digging through the contents has become an enjoyable experience in itself. Keys and memories alike are unearthed from the depths of the bag, each one revealing a story or a moment in time. The oversized aesthetic is not limited to bags alone; it has also given rise to gigantic jewelry pieces and accessories that are making waves on social media platforms. One individual's supersized creations have garnered significant attention online, with giant hair clips, wired earbuds, studded belts, and jumbo pins being just a few examples of her oversized offerings. The appeal of these oversized items lies in the nostalgia and whimsy they evoke when viewed through a campy lens. It's as if each item has become a vessel for memories and meaning, inviting the wearer or owner to reminisce about the past while also making a bold statement in the present. articles.title: Gstaad Palace's Refined Breakfast Experience Contrasts with Some American Hotels
articles.summary: A hotel's breakfast can reveal a lot about its hospitality standards, often more so than its luxurious rooms or marble lobby.
articles.content: A hotel's breakfast can reveal a lot about its hospitality standards, often more so than its luxurious rooms or marble lobby. While American hotels have made significant strides in creating elaborate breakfast buffets, they often fall short of providing a truly thoughtful experience for their guests. This can be attributed to the fact that guests are frequently presented with a standard spread of scrambled eggs under heat lamps and mediocre bacon, accompanied by an unexpectedly high price tag - think $38 per meal. At Gstaad Palace in Switzerland, breakfast is a refined affair where attention to detail is evident from start to finish. At Gstaad Palace in Switzerland, breakfast is a refined affair where attention to detail is evident from start to finish. A guest's name is not just checked off a list, but also used as an opportunity for personalization. This subtle touch sets the tone for a more bespoke experience. In contrast, some American hotels seem to prioritize quantity over quality, offering an overwhelming array of options that can be confusing rather than indulgent. Guests are left feeling processed and unattended to, rather than truly cared for. A hostess might take a guest's name, but it's the little gestures in between that make all the difference. Nick Hatsatouris, owner of Caffé Tusk at the Evelyn Hotel in New York City, notes that great breakfasts often involve something more straightforward and uncomplicated. He emphasizes the importance of focusing on what truly matters, not just heaping on more food, but creating an experience that leaves a lasting impression. In contrast to many American hotels, where a separate breakfast charge is often tacked on to an already steep room rate, European establishments tend to offer more inclusive dining experiences. The focus in Europe is not just about piling on as much food as possible but rather creating a thoughtful and authentic experience that leaves a lasting impression on guests. At Gleneagles in Scotland, the Scullery serves up local specialties like charcuterie, house-made sausages, haggis, and freshly prepared eggs and pancakes. A key aspect of successful hotel breakfasts is their ability to reflect the local culture and environment where they're located, as seen at Adare Manor in Ireland with its 132-foot-long gallery serving Irish breads, cheeses, and hot dishes. The typical American hotel breakfast often prioritizes quantity over quality, focusing on eggs, potatoes, bacon, and sausage, which can be overwhelming for guests. This emphasis on rich ingredients is a far cry from what many European hotels offer, where lighter preparations and fresh local produce take center stage. A well-stocked buffet with an array of options may seem appealing, but it's the simple things that truly make a hotel breakfast stand out: good coffee, freshly prepared dishes using local ingredients, and a warm welcome from staff. By stripping back the complexity and focusing on what really matters, hotels can create a more authentic and enjoyable dining experience for their guests. articles.title: Falfurrias Capital Partners Invests in Freeman & Forrest
articles.summary: Private equity firm Falfurrias Capital Partners has made a significant investment in Freeman & Forrest, an influencer marketing company.
articles.content: Private equity firm Falfurrias Capital Partners has made a significant investment in Freeman & Forrest, an influencer marketing company that specializes in reaching tech-savvy customers for big brands. The deal marks a major move by private equity into the creator economy, where companies are increasingly looking to leverage influencers and content creators to reach their target audiences. Freeman & Forrest plans to use the new investment to expand its services to more big tech companies and emerging startups in AI and cloud computing. The company also aims to break into other business-to-business (B2B) sectors such as healthcare and defense. The deal will see cofounder Emily Freeman remain at the helm as CEO, while cofounder Forrest Brazeal takes on a president role; both will join the board of directors along with new additions Alex Jutkowitz and Linda Boff. The influencer marketing company's financials are impressive, with an estimated annual revenue of around $50 million according to industry insiders. Freeman emphasized that the company's rapid growth would be further accelerated by the influx of capital, allowing it to expand its team more quickly and efficiently by hiring specialized staff for account management and software development. This investment is part of a broader trend in which private equity firms are increasingly backing creator economy companies as they mature, reflecting growing recognition of their potential for growth and returns on investment. Investors are pouring money into the sector: Quartermast estimates that PE-backed deals now make up around 8% of all creator economy investments so far this year, a significant increase from the usual 5% share. As companies seek to build trust with their clients, influencer marketing is becoming a crucial tool for enterprise B2B businesses. According to Forrester's predictions, by 2026 nearly three-quarters of these enterprises will be increasing their influencer budgets as trusted subject-matter experts take on greater importance in purchasing decisions. Freeman notes that B2B influencer marketing differs from its consumer-facing counterpart due to the emphasis on expertise rather than personality. In contrast to consumer products, where marketers often see an immediate impact on purchase decisions, B2B sales cycles can be lengthy and require a more educational approach to content creation. articles.title: Chicago's Missing-Middle Housing Types Widespread Across City
articles.summary: A new study has found that over a third of buildings in Chicago are mid-density housing, including duplexes, townhouses, and multiplexes.
articles.content: A new study has shed light on a crucial aspect of Chicago's housing landscape: the widespread presence of "missing-middle" housing types that don't fit neatly into existing zoning categories. The research, led by Arianna Salazar-Miranda, assistant professor of urban planning and data science at Yale School of the Environment, focused on mapping this often-overlooked segment of Chicago's building stock. The team's findings reveal a surprising prevalence of mid-density housing across the city, with over one-third of detected buildings fitting into this category. Duplexes are by far the most common type of missing-middle housing in Chicago, making up 36% of these buildings, followed closely by townhouses at 21%, and multiplexes at 17%. These units are typically found in older neighborhoods located between three to four miles from downtown. The concentration of middle housing in these areas is notable, as it suggests that existing zoning regulations may not be adequately accommodating the needs of Chicago's residents. Moreover, the research indicates a correlation between this type of housing and lower rent burdens, highlighting its potential as a solution to affordability issues in the city. The zoning regulations in many neighborhoods are not aligned with the existing housing stock, leading to inefficiencies and limitations on development. According to researchers, 41% of mid-density housing buildings in Chicago are located in areas zoned for single-family housing, which means that these buildings cannot be easily replicated or replaced. This discrepancy highlights the need for more flexible zoning policies that accommodate the diverse range of housing types already present in the city. The research team used an artificial intelligence model to analyze Google Street View photos and identify the type of housing stock in different areas of Chicago. The approach has the potential to be adapted for use in other cities, where it could help planners and policymakers better understand the relationship between zoning regulations and existing housing stock. However, one challenge to implementing this methodology is that building types can vary significantly from region to region, making it difficult to develop a standardized approach that can be applied uniformly across different metropolitan areas. The study's findings have significant implications for urban planning and policy-making in Chicago. By identifying areas where zoning laws are not being enforced, policymakers can develop targeted strategies to address these discrepancies. A standardized approach is needed to ensure consistency across the city, but this is a challenge due to the varying building types found in different regions. articles.title: Technological Change Leaves Bosses Out of Touch with Workers
articles.summary: Workers believe their bosses are out of touch with technological change's impact on jobs and lives.
articles.content: Leaders around the world would do well to take heed of a disturbing finding from recent research: nearly 4 in 5 workers believe their bosses are out of touch with the impact of technological change on their jobs and lives. The second phase of the AI debate is underway, shifting from speculation about its potential benefits and drawbacks to a more practical examination of how organizations can harness its power to drive lasting productivity gains and resilience. However, turning AI into a sustained competitive advantage will require much more than simply deploying new tools or systems; it demands a fundamental rethink of the way work is designed, staffed, and governed. Leaders who fail to adapt and lead their people through this transformation risk being left behind by more agile competitors, while those that succeed in harnessing AI's potential will reap significant rewards and create lasting value for their organizations. The data suggests that despite dire predictions about widespread job losses, the reality is more nuanced: employment rates remain healthy across most developed economies, with many companies still at the early stages of their AI journey, experimenting and searching for opportunities to create value. The narrative of widespread job losses due to AI has been somewhat exaggerated, but it's not a negligible phenomenon either. In fact, entry-level hiring in sectors exposed to AI, particularly software and customer service, is facing significant pressure. However, there are also positive signals emerging from our data, which covers 23 different markets worldwide. Over the past nine months, we've seen a notable shift in demand for certain types of workers: while entry-level placements in AI-exposed functions declined by 2.2% year on year, highly skilled white-collar profiles saw a surge in demand of 28%. A successful people strategy must navigate this dual reality, acknowledging that work is not disappearing entirely, yet recognizing the urgent need to adapt to rapidly changing tasks, skills, and career pathways. History provides valuable lessons here: general-purpose technologies like steam power, electricity, and information technology transformed productivity only when businesses reimagined their workflows, jobs, and management practices around them. As companies increasingly adopt artificial intelligence, a significant gap is emerging between technological progress and workforce readiness. This disparity threatens to hinder productivity gains and slow down transformation efforts. The World Economic Forum has projected that by 2030, nearly six out of every ten workers will require training to adapt to changing job requirements. Of those, about two-thirds can be upskilled within their current roles with the right support, while others may need to transition into new opportunities or risk being left behind. Upskilling and reskilling are becoming crucial components of a company's strategy for navigating the AI-driven workplace. The Adecco Group has extensive experience in providing training services, which allows it to witness firsthand the challenges that workers face during this period of transformation. Cultural resistance and workforce readiness have become significant obstacles to the widespread adoption of AI technology. Effective leadership will be required to overcome these hurdles and ensure a smooth transition for both employees and organizations. The pace at which companies are embracing AI often outstrips their employees' understanding and confidence in its applications, creating a readiness gap that can impede progress. This discrepancy has severe consequences for productivity and the overall success of organizational transformations. Organizations risk losing momentum if they fail to provide workers with the necessary support and education to thrive in an AI-driven environment. Our research highlights the disconnect between employee openness to change and management's ability to facilitate it, revealing a critical gap in communication and involvement. The uneven distribution of AI benefits is a growing concern. Workers who have undergone training on how to work alongside AI are more likely to feel at ease in these environments, with some experiencing a significant boost in comfort levels. However, this advantage does not extend to all employees. Those excluded from the redesign of their roles and responsibilities tend to be less open to adapting to change, highlighting a disconnect between management's ability to facilitate change and employee openness to it. The leadership bottleneck is evident in the low percentage of workers who feel that concerns about new technologies are taken seriously by their employers. This lack of consideration for employees' anxieties can have serious consequences for organizations struggling to adapt to AI-driven changes. To truly succeed, companies must move beyond treating productivity and people as competing objectives. Instead, they should view AI as a catalyst for operating model transformation, one that involves reshaping work around human strengths and fostering continuous learning and mobility. Investors, meanwhile, are being forced to redefine what it means for an organization to be mature in its use of AI. No longer can implementation be measured solely by technology spend or adoption rates; instead, the focus should shift to measurable business impact, workforce agility, and skills resilience. Redesigning work processes is crucial before automating tasks, as it helps identify areas where people create value and where AI can augment or automate tasks. To maximize the benefits of automation, businesses must focus on building skills that are relevant to real-world career opportunities. Training programs without a clear pathway for applying new skills will fall short in preparing workers for an increasingly automated future. Effective implementation requires more than just technological know-how; leaders must also involve their employees in the change process, providing transparency about what's changing and giving them a stake in redesigning their work processes. Ultimately, the defining characteristic of this generation's leadership will be their ability to harmonize human and digital intelligence, leveraging AI to enhance productivity, resilience, and the human touch. articles.title: NFL teams benefit from having a star quarterback on a rookie contract
articles.summary: Having a top-performing quarterback on a rookie contract can provide financial flexibility for NFL teams and lead to long-term success.
articles.content: The financial flexibility provided by having a star quarterback on a rookie contract can be a game-changer for NFL teams. The New England Patriots' recent success is a testament to this, as they made it all the way to the Super Bowl last year. The Chicago Bears are also poised to make a deep playoff run in 2026. To maximize the benefits of having a quarterback on a rookie contract, however, that player must be exceptional. Drake Maye nearly became the league MVP last season, and Caleb Williams is currently in contention for the award this year. These two quarterbacks, along with a few others, are likely to receive massive contract extensions when they become eligible. For teams struggling with underperforming young quarterbacks, the picture is much bleaker. They often find themselves with plenty of cap space to spend on other positions but lack a reliable signal-caller at the most crucial spot. This can lead to a quarterback's career fizzling out and the team being forced to look elsewhere for their franchise face. The pressure is mounting for teams with struggling quarterbacks, as they risk wasting valuable draft picks or free agent signings if they don't find a solution soon. A few teams might be facing this exact scenario in the coming months. Caleb Williams has been one of the standout performers on rookie contracts so far, and his impressive play has put him firmly in contention for a massive contract extension. With two years of experience under his belt, Williams is already making waves in the league. Drake Maye achieved an unprecedented feat last season by reaching the Super Bowl, despite being just in his second year as a pro. His incredible performance earned him a spot among the league's top quarterbacks, and he remains one of the most promising young players in the game. Maye's impressive start to his career has been somewhat overshadowed by a disappointing third season, marked by high turnover numbers and an underwhelming record. However, some of this can be attributed to the Patriots' roster being decimated by injuries, which may have contributed to Maye's struggles. The uncertainty surrounding Maye's next contract is palpable, given his recent ankle injury in Week 10 and a lackluster third season. Despite these setbacks, there is no denying that he remains the Patriots' clear choice for quarterback of the present and future. Maye's proven track record far surpasses that of any other quarterback on a rookie deal, making him a highly sought-after commodity when it comes to contract extensions. His upside is undeniable, and teams will be eager to secure his services in the coming months. C.J. Stroud's resurgence this season has been a welcome sight for the Houston Texans, who are desperately trying to stay in contention for a playoff spot. His impressive performance has made him a prime candidate for a massive contract extension. Stroud's numbers this year are eerily similar to those that earned him Offensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2023. He leads the league in passing yards per game and interception rate, mirroring his standout rookie season. The Texans' decision to sign Stroud to a lucrative extension will be based on their assessment of his entire career trajectory. They will likely view the campaigns bookending his four-year tenure as more indicative of what's to come than the mediocre seasons in between. Cam Ward's future with the Tennessee Titans remains uncertain, despite being drafted first overall last year. The team is facing a critical juncture, weighing whether to stick with Ward or draft another quarterback and rebuild around him. The Titans' willingness to trade key players like Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker suggests they're prioritizing developing their young talent over making quick fixes. This approach implies that they believe Ward has potential, but need time to see it unfold. Tennessee's decision to retain Tony Pollard and consistently add depth at wide receiver further underscores their commitment to giving Ward every opportunity to succeed. The next eight games will be a crucial test of whether this strategy pays off or if the team needs to look elsewhere for quarterback help. The Denver Broncos have been masters of winning close games, thanks in large part to Bo Nix's heroics. He led the league in game-winning drives last year and continues to excel under pressure, with six game-winning drives this season. Nix's ability to deliver in crunch time has been a key factor in the Broncos' success. However, his team would benefit from him being more consistent throughout games, rather than relying on late-game heroics. While Nix is having an impressive season, it's worth noting that his team's overall performance leaves much to be desired. The Broncos struggle to put up points early, which puts unnecessary pressure on their quarterback to perform in the final minutes. The Denver Broncos' quarterback situation has been a mixed bag this season, with some promising signs emerging from the struggles of Russell Nix. Despite his slow start to the year, Nix's last three games have shown improvement, and he might be rounding back into form just in time for the crucial stretch run. Nix's overall performance is still below par compared to his previous two seasons, but it's worth noting that some of this regression could be attributed to the change in play-calling duties after Week 5. Sean Payton took over as offensive coordinator, which might have affected Nix's ability to perform at his best. Despite some ups and downs early on, Russell Nix has been a valuable asset to the Broncos since joining them in 2024. His potential is evident, especially considering he might have played in the Super Bowl last postseason if not for an ankle injury. The team will likely continue to invest in Nix as his career progresses, given his impressive performance so far. The question remains whether he can maintain this level of play and lead the Broncos to success. Fernando Mendoza's debut as a starter was a mixed bag, with six sacks taken and a modest 17-of-29 completion rate. However, he did manage to score his first touchdown on a 10-yard run to the end zone against the Seattle Seahawks' formidable defense. To succeed in the long term, Mendoza will need more robust support from his teammates, particularly in terms of wide receivers. The Las Vegas Raiders might consider bolstering their receiver group in the coming months to give him the necessary tools to excel. In contrast, J.J. McCarthy's fortunes have changed significantly since joining the New York Giants five weeks ago. After struggling with injuries and inconsistent play during his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings, he has found new life under the Giants' coaching staff. McCarthy's performances in recent games have been impressive, including a standout 243-yard fourth quarter. Since earning the starting job, he has completed 66.3% of his passes for an average of 224 yards per game, accompanied by one touchdown and one interception. The New York Giants are reaping the benefits of McCarthy's resurgence, with a 2-1 record in games where he started as quarterback. His presence has helped maintain their lead in the NFC East so far, which is more than what they could have reasonably expected from his trade. McCarthy still has areas to improve upon, but it's clear that the change in scenery has revitalized his career and given him a second chance at success. The road ahead for McCarthy appears uncertain, but there's still a chance he could prove himself as a starting-caliber quarterback and secure another opportunity in 2027. With Jaxson Dart set to return next year, it's possible McCarthy will be relegated to backup duty, focusing on development rather than being the primary starter. Jayden Daniels' impressive rookie season was marked by an elbow dislocation and lower-body injuries that hindered his progress. Despite this, he has shown flashes of brilliance when healthy, but his overall production has been limited due to playing only 14 games since 2024. Daniels' team, the Washington Commanders, has struggled despite his efforts, with a mediocre record of 4-9-1 over the last two seasons. His remarkable rookie season was followed by a mixed bag of performances, including some outstanding individual achievements and disappointing team results. The Commanders' quarterback's rushing abilities have waned somewhat since his impressive rookie campaign, but he has become a more accurate passer this year. He currently leads the league in interception rate and is on track to set a new career high in yards per game. Daniels' performance has been affected by the lack of support around him, particularly on the offensive line and at wide receiver. If the Commanders can strengthen these areas, he may be able to recapture his 2024 form and solidify himself as a top-tier quarterback. Despite individual inconsistencies, Daniels is not the main issue in Washington. The team's overall performance has been hindered by various factors, including injuries and lack of depth. The Bears' surge up the Super Bowl rankings can be attributed in part to Caleb Williams' rapid ascent into stardom. Individually, Williams is showing tremendous promise, with a trajectory that could one day lead him to an MVP award. From a team perspective, Williams' emergence as a top quarterback has been instrumental in propelling the Bears toward the front of the Super Bowl race. His individual success is driving the team's overall improvement and pushing them towards the pinnacle of NFL competition. The third-year quarterback's recent four-interception outing was an isolated incident in what has been a breakout season for him. Prior to that setback, he had shown significant improvement in the high-octane offense of Ben Johnson and had taken care of the ball with remarkable efficiency. This season, he is putting up career-best numbers, including a top-notch passer rating and impressive sack avoidance. His ability to perform under pressure has been a key factor in his success this year. With an average of 257.7 passing yards per game, he has established himself as one of the most reliable quarterbacks in the league. This level of performance is not only a testament to his skills but also a boost for his team's overall chances. The quarterback's growth has been nothing short of remarkable, and it feels like this could be the start of a truly special career. His ability to read defenses and make split-second decisions on the field has improved dramatically over the past year. As he continues to develop, there is no doubt that he will be one of the top quarterbacks in the league. The second quarter of the season saw a slight dip in performance from Bryce Young, but overall, this remains his best year yet. With his team facing crucial decisions on his contract status, it's more important than ever for him to continue delivering at an elite level. His ability to adapt to different situations and make key plays when needed has been a hallmark of his game. Under the guidance of Coach Dave Canales, Young has taken significant strides in improving his skills and understanding the nuances of the game. His coach seems to have a deep appreciation for Young's abilities and knows exactly how to utilize them effectively. As a result, Young has consistently delivered high-level performances when called upon. One area where Young excels is in terms of yardage production. This season, he averages an impressive 266.3 yards per game, far surpassing his previous career-best campaign. His ability to stretch defenses and make big plays down the field has been a key factor in his team's success. While Young still experiences down weeks, his overall development has been steady and on track. He remains one of the most promising young quarterbacks in the league, and his team is fortunate to have him as their signal-caller. As he continues to grow and mature, there is no doubt that he will be a key factor in his team's success for years to come. The New Orleans Saints are known for their aggressive approach on offense, and they have found a quarterback who can execute that style effectively. Coach Kellen Moore has put a lot of responsibility on Tyler Shough's plate over the past year and a half, and he has responded with solid performances. Despite his team's struggles on defense, Shough has managed to keep them competitive in their division. With a strong connection to rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran Chris Olave, he will continue to be a vital component of the Saints' offense going forward. As he gains more experience and develops his skills further, it will become clearer whether he is truly a franchise quarterback. Michael Penix Jr.'s career has been marked by inconsistency, making it challenging to evaluate his overall impact. The torn ACL he suffered last season and the Atlanta Falcons' handling of their quarterback room in the previous year are factors that cannot be held against him. Despite having a talented supporting cast on offense, the team's success hinges on its quarterback's performance. Over 20 starts, Penix has shown an average to slightly below-average level of play, which is what will be graded. articles.title: Russian Forces Use Drones to Guide Infiltration Teams Through Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian defenses are being breached by small teams of soldiers who infiltrate between enemy positions using drones for navigation assistance.
articles.content: Russian forces have been employing a stealthy tactic to breach Ukrainian defenses, using small teams of soldiers who infiltrate between enemy positions to create chaos. These infiltration teams are often sent to slip in undetected, where they can disrupt Ukrainian supply lines and isolate outposts by reporting back to their units on troop-rotation routes. The use of drones has become a key component in guiding these small groups through the front line, providing them with crucial navigation assistance, especially at night when visibility is low. However, this tactic has its limitations, as the presence of drones can sometimes inadvertently reveal the approach of Russian forces to Ukrainian units. The use of drones by Russian forces has been observed guiding infiltration teams through Ukrainian territory. Reconnaissance drones fly above or slightly ahead of infantrymen, providing real-time visual guidance to commanders via radio communications. The feed from these drones is used to direct the movement of troops, specifying turns and next steps. However, this tactic can inadvertently alert Ukrainian units to the presence of enemy forces. When drones are used in this way, they sometimes serve as a telltale sign, revealing the approach of Russian groups to Ukrainian positions. This has been observed by both sides in combat situations. Russian infiltration teams also rely on GPS coordinates and drones to navigate through hostile territory. According to Volodymyr Golyagin, head of a communications department, prisoners have revealed that they are taught to recognize their own side's drones, which guide them along designated routes. Once they reach their destination, Russian forces switch to radio communication, attempting to evade Ukrainian FPV drones. In some cases, Russian groups use abandoned or damaged structures for shelter, targeting these locations with drone crews. Golyagin noted that once the teams are on the ground, they are left to fend for themselves, dodging attempts by Ukrainian FPV drones to strike them. As Ukrainian forces attempt to intercept and neutralize Russian infiltration teams, they face a challenge in detecting these small groups before they reach their targets. The Russian troops have adapted by using concealment tools such as thermal-imaging cloaks to remain undetected. According to Yabchanka's estimates, approximately 90% of enemy infantry are eliminated while still approaching the Ukrainian positions. This high success rate is a testament to the effectiveness of the combined efforts of intelligence gathering and precision strikes. The use of guide drones has become an essential component in this strategy. Kateryna Stepanenko, the Russia team lead at the Institute for the Study of War, notes that the employment of guide drones represents an evolution of earlier tactics. In these earlier instances, drones were used to gather intelligence and direct artillery fire, but now their role extends beyond mere reconnaissance. They provide critical support to infiltrators by offering real-time information on terrain, enemy positions, and potential threats. The reliance on guide drones poses a significant risk, however, as their presence can inadvertently reveal troop positions on the ground. This vulnerability makes it essential for Russian forces to carefully balance the benefits of using these drones against the potential costs. articles.title: Electrochemical Sensor Developed Using Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University have made significant progress in developing an ultrasensitive electrochemical sensor for detecting extremely low concentrations of vitamin C.
articles.content: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University have made significant progress in developing an ultrasensitive electrochemical sensor for detecting extremely low concentrations of vitamin C. The breakthrough was achieved by incorporating artificial intelligence into the sensor development process, allowing the team to identify promising fabrication conditions with limited experimental data. The use of AI in this context enabled the researchers to streamline the optimization process, reducing the need for extensive trial-and-error experimentation that is often required when developing sensitive electrochemical sensors. By leveraging the capabilities of AI, the team was able to pinpoint the most effective fabrication conditions, thereby accelerating the development of the sensor. Vitamin C plays a crucial role in antioxidant protection and immune function, making it essential to accurately measure its levels in the blood. However, conventional analytical techniques often require sophisticated equipment, which can be limiting for widespread use. The new electrochemical sensor aims to address these challenges by providing a more accessible and efficient means of detecting vitamin C. The researchers employed a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) material in their design, which is capable of selectively recognizing vitamin C molecules. This specialized material enables the sensor to detect even trace amounts of vitamin C, making it an invaluable tool for assessing nutritional status. The team behind this innovative sensor design employed a materials-informed approach to optimize its performance. By matching the molecular structure of the target molecule, vitamin C, with specific recognition sites in the material, they created a precise fit. To further refine their design, researchers combined this material with artificial intelligence-based machine learning algorithms. This powerful combination enabled them to predict the optimal fabrication conditions for producing high-performance sensors. The optimization process focused on four critical parameters: material concentrations, electrochemical polymerization cycles, solution pH, and their interactions. By evaluating these variables at multiple levels, they generated a vast array of possible combinations, 625 in total, from which to choose. Using machine learning, the team trained an algorithm with data from 25 initial experiments, allowing it to pinpoint promising conditions that had not been tested previously. The recommended settings were then used to fabricate sensors, which were subsequently validated through experimental testing. The study's findings have significant implications for the development of sensors that can detect disease-related biomarkers and environmental pollutants at extremely low concentrations. Researchers are now planning to expand the use of AI in sensor design beyond optimizing fabrication conditions, with a focus on recommending suitable sensing materials for specific target molecules. This could lead to the creation of highly sensitive sensors capable of detecting even minute amounts of substances. The ultimate goal is to develop sensors that can identify and quantify disease-related biomarkers and environmental pollutants at concentrations as low as parts per trillion, paving the way for early detection and treatment of diseases and improved environmental monitoring. articles.title: Azzedine Alaïa Exhibition Opens at San Francisco's Legion of Honor Museum
articles.summary: The exhibition showcases Azzedine Alaïa's iconic designs and highlights his use of innovative fabrics created by Italian knitwear specialists.
articles.content: A major exhibition dedicated to the late Tunisian fashion designer Azzedine Alaïa has opened at San Francisco's Legion of Honor museum, showcasing the human touch behind his iconic designs. The exhibition, "Sculpting Fashion, is a testament to Alaïa's mastery of construction and his ability to make the body look better. Model Veronica Webb once described him as someone who no one anywhere in the world can touch in terms of his skills. The show isn't about rejecting modern technology; rather it highlights Alaïa's use of tools like Italian knitwear specialists to create innovative fabrics. As Carla Sozzani, president of the Fondation Azzedine Alaïa, notes, he was fascinated by new technologies, including the telephone when it first emerged. The exhibition is a carefully curated selection of Alaïa's work, put together by Laura L. Camerlengo from the Legion of Honor and Olivier Saillard, director of the designer's foundation. It marks the first American retrospective of his designs, and comes ahead of the tenth anniversary of his passing in 2017. Alaïa had a connection to San Francisco, having received an honorary doctorate from the Academy of Art University in 2005, and had previously visited the Legion of Honor museum. The exhibition adheres to a protocol established by Alaïa before his passing, which is carefully followed by Saillard and the foundation. These mannequins have been designed without heads, but they are based on Naomi Campbell's body measurements, taken from garments created specifically for her. Their placement on raised plinths imbues them with an air of grandeur, drawing attention to the craftsmanship that goes into each piece. Fashion exhibitions often feature garments as standalone objects, rather than part of a larger display, Alaïa's work is no exception. A stunning beaded black and red dress has been situated among paintings from the 15th century, including one with intricate details from a Spanish palace. In stark contrast to Alaïa's fluid designs, the surrounding arrangements evoke a sense of Grecian order and precision. The exhibition reveals the designer's fascination with the divine feminine, a theme that transcends time due to his unconventional approach to fashion. His clothes cannot be dated, Alaïa once observed in a statement that speaks volumes about his artistic philosophy. Born in Tunisia in 1935, Alaïa was drawn to the arts from an early age and initially enrolled at the École des Beaux Arts school in Tunis to study sculpture when he was just 15. The exhibition at San Francisco's Legion of Honor museum showcases a selection of designs on loan from various institutions, displayed in separate rooms alongside Alaïa's own work. He believed true innovation required an understanding of the past, says Camerlengo, highlighting Alaïa's commitment to drawing from historical influences. This approach is particularly relevant today, as technological advancements disrupt traditional notions of fashion and art. The Rodin gallery features a striking display where two column dresses are juxtaposed with a sculpture of a massive hand, illustrating Alaïa's connection to the artistic traditions he admired. It reminds me that Azzedine spent his life doing something with his hands, notes Saillard, emphasizing the designer's hands-on approach. The second room explores Alaïa's relationship with America, including his 1982 in-store show at Bergdorf Goodman, which was a groundbreaking success. Camerlengo explains how Alaïa's designs spoke to a more assertive and sexualized expression of feminism in the 80s, marking a shift from the previous decade's emphasis on fitting in. The exhibition Sculpting Fashion" features a remarkable collection of Azzedine Alaïa's designs that showcase his fascination with various cultures and historical periods. The designer's spring 1992 collection was inspired by Madame du Pompadour, the mistress of Louis XV, who had previously lived in the building where Alaïa resided. The exhibition's next room is a testament to the mastery of couture techniques, while also highlighting the influence of non-European cultures on Alaïa's work. The designer's use of cut leathers and latticework screens, reminiscent of North African mashirabya, is just one example of this eclectic approach. The exhibition concludes with a room dedicated to all-out glamour, reflecting Alaïa's early love of cinema, which was sparked by his grandparents' frequent trips to the movies. The show will run from November 21, 2026 through April 11, 2027 at the Legion of Honor. articles.title: Kerch Bridge Suffers Significant Damage in Ukrainian Aerial Attack
articles.summary: Ukraine's latest strike on the Kerch Bridge has disrupted rail traffic between Russia and Crimea.
articles.content: A crucial transportation link between Russia and Crimea was severely disrupted after Ukraine launched its third aerial attack on the Kerch Bridge in just four days. The latest strike brought rail traffic to a halt across the 19-kilometer span, which connects mainland Russia to the peninsula that Moscow annexed from Ukraine in 2014. Russian authorities were forced to assess the damage and temporarily suspend train services while repairs were underway. According to Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, rail traffic was expected to resume by around 4 p.m. local time on Thursday, although it remained unclear when the road section would be fully operational again. The Ukrainian strikes coincided with a high-stakes diplomatic meeting in China between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his counterparts from the US and China. The attacks served as a stark reminder that Ukraine still holds significant leverage in the conflict and undermines Moscow's claims of inevitable victory. As international leaders gathered for talks in Berlin, including US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders, the Kerch Bridge remained a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea. A significant portion of the road deck and an arch on the Kerch Bridge were severely damaged in this week's attack, which was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes carried out over seven stages, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The latest assault used domestically produced Neptune missiles, causing damage to the train track, as confirmed by Ukraine's Defense Ministry. This development will likely cause disruption to fuel and ammunition supplies, which Russia will now need to reroute overland, where Ukrainian drones are waiting to intercept them. Russia's air defenses reportedly intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones across 10 regions during the night, according to a statement from the Russian Defense Ministry. Meanwhile, Ukraine claimed that Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at its territory, with hits recorded at 18 locations. The impact of these strikes was felt beyond the military front, with Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announcing that at least 10 people were wounded in Russian attacks on 12 regions. Damage was reported in various areas, a testament to Russia's continued reliance on strategic bombing tactics. As Ukraine continues to hold its ground against the Russian army's numerical superiority, Kyiv's defenses are being bolstered by domestically developed long-range drones and missiles that have been striking deep inside Russian territory, often targeting oil refineries. Ukrainian officials are increasingly concerned that their country's fate may be decided by agreements between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, a notion that has sparked unease among European governments. Meanwhile, in an effort to isolate Putin diplomatically, European leaders have imposed severe economic sanctions on Russia, while also attempting to maintain a united front against Moscow's aggressive actions. Britain's Prince Harry recently expressed his own views on the matter, stating in an interview that he believes there is a significant disconnect between the Trump administration's stance on Ukraine and the opinions of the American people. The relationship between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has also been strained, with reports suggesting that Trump has referred to Putin as his "friend" in private conversations. The security arrangements being discussed by European leaders are aimed at preventing a repeat of Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Kyiv wants to guarantee that its borders remain secure without NATO military presence nearby, while Moscow seeks to keep the alliance away from its own borders. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is set to host French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham among other leaders for this meeting. The meeting will also explore how Ukraine's European backers can fit into postwar security arrangements. articles.title: US Employers Wary of AI-Generated Job Applications
articles.summary: A recent survey by Greenhouse found that 90% of US employers believe they've been misled by AI-generated resumes.
articles.content: Hiring managers have become increasingly wary of AI-generated job applications, with nine in ten US employers believing they've rejected real candidates because their applications appeared fake or artificial. A survey by Greenhouse found that 90% of employers think they've been misled by AI-generated resumes, although it's unclear whether these employers use AI detection tools to identify such applications. The company has not clarified how many respondents reported using such tools versus simply relying on intuition. Many employers are responding to the rise of AI in job applications by tweaking their hiring processes. In fact, 86% of those surveyed said they've made changes to account for AI's impact on recruitment. One common adjustment is adding an extra human interview step - a move taken by 57% of respondents. As job seekers increasingly rely on AI to perfect and send out their applications, employers are struggling to distinguish genuine candidates from those generated by algorithms. According to the report, hiring teams are caught in an ongoing tug-of-war with applicants, both trying to stay ahead in the game. Employers are increasingly relying on AI-powered resume screening tools to weed out unsuitable applicants, but these automated systems often reject resumes that are too polished or overly formatted for their own good. As a result, job seekers are trying various tactics to get past the screening process, including exaggerating their skills and hiding text in their resumes aimed at fooling the AI reviewers. However, this approach is not only seen as untrustworthy but also ineffective, with employers growing wary of applicants who resort to such tactics. According to a recent report, 81% of employers have witnessed job seekers attempting to outsmart the system by claiming skills they don't actually possess or using creative formatting to make their resumes more AI-friendly. However, this strategy often backfires and ends up raising suspicions among recruiters. The growing reliance on AI-powered hiring tools is also making it difficult for applicants to stand out in a crowded job market, as employers increasingly use these systems to filter candidates and have early conversations with promising prospects through voice technology. A growing number of employers are using voice AI in their hiring processes, but a significant majority reject resumes that resemble those generated by artificial intelligence. The survey of 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across five countries found that half of those who use voice AI believe the early-stage candidate experience has improved. However, what constitutes an "improved" experience remains unclear, leaving room for interpretation on whether applicants would agree with this assessment. A separate study suggests that job seekers are not necessarily opposed to AI-powered interviews, as only 7% in the US would decline such an opportunity. Moreover, 70% of those who have undergone live AI interviews report that it helped them demonstrate their skills effectively. The findings may be influenced by the current state of the US job market, which has been challenging for applicants despite a better-than-expected October job report. As employers increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to screen job applicants, a crucial decision-making process remains firmly in human hands. According to recent findings, human oversight is still prevalent in key hiring decisions, despite AI's growing presence in the recruitment process. Deciding which candidates to advance to the next stage of the hiring process is one task that employers are hesitant to hand over to AI agents, with only 7% of tasks being automated. A California law aims to safeguard employees from being unfairly terminated by AI systems making performance assessments without human input. The use of artificial intelligence in hiring processes raises questions about its effectiveness in capturing the essence of an applicant's interview. While AI systems can provide a more uniform and efficient screening process, they may not accurately gauge a candidate's personality or fit for a role. Greenhouse CEO Daniel Chait suggests that one way to address this issue is by opening up voice AI interviews to all applicants, allowing more people to have a real conversation with the company sooner. He argues that this can help increase the number of candidates who reach an interview stage, currently only three in every 100 applications. Scaling up hiring processes through AI may provide a solution to the current bottleneck, but it is also worth considering the complementary role of human interviews in the process. articles.title: Choosing the Right Sweet Potato at the Store
articles.summary: When selecting sweet potatoes, look for ones with smooth skin and firm texture.
articles.content: Sweet potatoes have become a seasonal staple as fall arrives, offering a rich flavor and fluffy texture that's versatile in various recipes. From savory pies to aromatic curries, sweet potatoes are a culinary chameleon that can be enjoyed in many ways, whether roasted or served with generous amounts of butter. Despite their widespread popularity, choosing the right sweet potato at the store often goes unnoticed. When selecting sweet potatoes, it's essential to look for ones with smooth skin that is evenly colored. This is according to the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) extension, which emphasizes the importance of appearance in determining quality. A slight imperfection on the surface won't necessarily affect the taste or texture of the sweet potato, as long as it's firm and free from soft spots. "A little dirt or an odd shape is no big deal," says Choung. She adds that a gentle squeeze can help to identify any inconsistencies in the texture. However, deeper cuts or bruises may compromise the overall quality of the sweet potato. If you notice excessive sprouting, don't be alarmed, just snap off the sprouts before cooking and proceed as usual. When roasting multiple sweet potatoes at once, it's essential to choose ones that are roughly the same size so they cook evenly. This ensures that none of them become overcooked or undercooked, which can affect their texture and flavor. Sweet potato varieties come in a wide range of colors and flesh types, from the familiar orange-fleshed variety to Japanese and Korean drier starchier sweet potatoes with pale or deep purple flesh. When it comes to choosing a specific variety for roasting, Choung advises that any kind will do, but if you're making a recipe that calls for a particular type of sweet potato, use that one. When selecting a sweet potato variety for roasting, it's worth noting that there are many different types available in most grocery stores, including Garnet and Jewel. Some varieties may have specific characteristics or uses, but any type can be used for roasting. However, if a recipe calls for a particular type of sweet potato, it's best to use that one. Local farmers' markets often carry heirloom or less common sweet potato varieties, such as "fingerling" sweet potatoes, which are small but just as sweet as full-size ones. These smaller varieties may be worth trying for their unique flavor and texture. Meanwhile, Japanese and Korean sweet potatoes can have varying characteristics due to the multiple varieties they cover. Some popular white- or cream-fleshed sweet potato varieties include Hannah and White Triumph, while O'Henry is another option. When selecting sweet potatoes, it's essential to be vigilant about their condition before bringing them home. This means checking for visible signs of spoilage such as mold, deep cracks, or soft spots that could lead to food waste and potentially even foodborne illness. Variety is also key - don't limit yourself to the usual orange varieties, explore options like Japanese, Korean, purple-fleshed, and white-fleshed sweet potatoes which can add unique flavors and textures to your cooking.
